This whole metaphor could mean: (1) if Jesus and his disciples did God’s work during the limited time God had given him to work with them (the daytime), they would not fail (stumble) because Jesus was with them. In this metaphor Jesus uses the light to refer to himself, who has previously called himself “the Light of the World” in 8:12 and 9:5. This interpretation has a similar meaning to Jesus’ statement in 9:4; (2) someone who does not act according to God’s will (walks at night) is an unbeliever who fails completely (stumble) because that person does not know Jesus.

11:18: This verse gives background information about the place where this event took place.

This could mean: (1) they are asking to know the identity of the Son of Man; (2) they are asking to know what Jesus means when he says, “Son of Man.”

Jesus uses Walk to refer to how a person lives and behaves. He is telling the crowd to live and act according to the example that he has shown them while he has been with them.
Jesus uses darkness as though it were a person who could overtake someone.
Jesus uses darkness to refer to what is false and evil.
Jesus uses this phrase to refer to a person who lives a sinful life and behaves sinfully.

12:44: John uses cried out to imply that Jesus was speaking loudly to a crowd of people.

13:2: Here, put into the heart is an idiom that means to cause someone to think about something.
13:3: John uses hands to refer to power and authority.

ἦν γὰρ μεγάλη ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνου τοῦ Σαββάτου

Jesus uses my side to refer to the wound that a Roman soldier made in his side with a spear.
